fixes.explanation: A scorpion would get my attention, friend. I'd be up on the highest shelf in a second, gold base and all. But God names a different creature: “I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.” (Exodus 23:28). The hornet is the one He sends, and no scorpion shows up in that verse.

A prophet is a reasonable guess, friend, but God doesn't say prophet here. Listen to how He puts it: “Behold, I am sending an angel before you…” (Exodus 23:20). The one out front on this road is an angel, and that's the whole answer.

Turning back to Egypt is a creative guess, baker, but the verse never says the angel turns back anywhere. Egypt doesn't even come up. God's reason is that the angel “…will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.” (Exodus 23:21). The trouble is defying him, not a U-turn.

You got it, baker. God tells Israel, “…do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.” (Exodus 23:21). His Name is in the angel, and that's why the warning is so serious. When this messenger speaks, Israel is told to listen.

You got it, baker. God says, “But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.” (Exodus 23:22). Listening to the angel and doing everything God says go together. The promise comes with that “if.”

A sacrifice before every battle sounds devoted, friend, but this verse doesn't ask for one. God says, “…if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies…” (Exodus 23:22). No altar in sight. The ask is listening and obeying.

DEMOLISH. SMASH. God doesn't say “politely redecorate,” friend! After telling Israel not to bow down to those gods, He says, “Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.” (Exodus 23:24). I stamp cookies for a living, so swinging a hammer is way outside my lane. But the instruction is plain: those gods are not to be left alone.

That's the one, baker. God says, “I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.” (Exodus 23:27). Terror goes ahead, confusion hits every nation Israel encounters, and the enemies turn and run. That's one way to clear a path.

You got it, baker. God says, “For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.” (Exodus 23:31). He delivers them into Israel's hand, and Israel drives them out. Both parts sit in the same verse.

FALSE, and God leaves no loophole, friend. He says, “You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.” (Exodus 23:32). Look at that “or.” The covenant is off the table with the nations and with their gods, not just one of them. Asking for a covenant with only the people is like asking me for a cookie with no dough.
